rationale: Apparent Lycopolitan/scribal variant of ⲡⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ (Greek δίκαιος 'righteous'), with vowel-shift ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓ → ⲁⲓⲕⲁⲗ. Confirmed by antithetic pairing with ⲡⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'the Sinner' in the Picture-Book context. Could alternatively be read as a fusion ⲡ-ⲁⲓ-ⲕⲁⲗⲟⲥ ('the beautiful one'), but the soteriological context demands the legal-judicial 'righteous.'
Standard Manichaean technical term for Mani's Picture-Book (the Eikon, Mid. Persian Ardhang/Ārdahang), the painted scroll depicting the cosmic-soteriological order. Capitalized as a proper title.
Already in glossary as ⲣⲉϩ†ⲍⲉⲡ. Confirmed here in alternation with Greek ⲡⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ — both name the same cosmic judging figure who sentences souls after death.

proposed_english: and they cause to reach / cause to attain
rationale: Causative-conjunctive: ⲛ̄- (conjunctive prefix) + ⲩ̄ (Lyc. for ⲥⲉ '3pl') + ⲧⲉϩⲟ ('reach,' in glossary). 'And they cause-them-to-reach' — used soteriologically of the angelic/judicial conveyance of righteous souls to the Region of Light.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲙⲟⲩϩⲉ 'burn, scorch' (Crum 207b) — distinct from the homophone ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill.' Context (Gehenna, eschatological torment) confirms the burning sense.
Lycopolitan ⲙⲁⲁ = Sah. ⲙⲁ 'place,' with vocalic doubling. Standard place-noun used here for the appointed eschatological dwelling of the catechumen.
